taxonomy.subtopic: Preoperative alpha blockade before beta blockade

questions.stem_html:
A 37-year-old woman has recurrent episodes of pounding headache, palpitations, diaphoresis, and tremulousness. During one episode her blood pressure is 228/116 mm Hg. Plasma free metanephrines are elevated, and MRI reveals a 3-cm adrenal medullary mass. Surgery is planned after medical preparation.

Which medication sequence is most appropriate before tumor removal?

options.text_html: Begin a nonselective beta blocker first, then add an alpha blocker after heart rate normalizes
Establish alpha-adrenergic blockade and volume repletion before adding a beta blocker if tachycardia persists
Use a thiazide diuretic alone to reduce intravascular volume before surgery
Start an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor and avoid adrenergic antagonists
Administer atropine followed by a calcium-channel blocker only on the day of surgery

questions.explanation_html: Alpha blockade controls catecholamine-mediated vasoconstriction and permits intravascular volume restoration. Beta blockade may be added only afterward to control persistent tachycardia. Starting beta blockade first removes beta-2 vasodilation while alpha receptors remain active, risking an unopposed hypertensive crisis.

wrong_choice_explanations.1: Beta blockade before alpha blockade can leave unopposed alpha-mediated vasoconstriction and precipitate severe hypertension.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: These patients are often chronically volume contracted and require alpha blockade plus volume expansion, not further isolated volume depletion.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: ACE inhibition does not reliably protect against catecholamine surges during tumor manipulation.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Atropine may worsen tachycardia and does not provide the required preoperative alpha blockade.

questions.educational_objective: Apply the required preoperative sequence for pheochromocytoma: alpha blockade and volume expansion first, followed by beta blockade only when needed.
